question: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
solution:
Assuming the Sun to be a solid sphere, $I = \frac{2}{5}mR^2$

Using conservation of angular momentum, $I'\omega' = I\omega$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{5}m(2R)^2 \times \frac{2\pi}{T'} = \frac{2}{5}mR^2 \times \frac{2\pi}{T}$$
$$\Rightarrow T' = 4T = 4 \times 27 = 108\text{ days}$$

question:
Three identical heat conducting rods are connected in series as shown in the figure. The rods on the sides have thermal conductivity $2K$ while that in the middle has thermal conductivity $K$. The left end of the combination is maintained at temperature $3T$ and the right end at $T$. The rods are thermally insulated from outside. In steady state, temperature at the left junction is $T_1$ and that at the right junction is $T_2$. The ratio $T_1/T_2$ is

<image_1>
solution:
Sol. In series, $R_{\text{eq.}} = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$

$$= \frac{l}{2KA} + \frac{l}{KA} + \frac{l}{2KA}$$

$$= \frac{4l}{2KA}$$

$$R_{\text{eq.}} = \frac{2l}{KA}$$

In series rate of heat flow is same

$$\therefore \frac{3T - T_1}{R_1} = \frac{3T - T}{R_{\text{eq.}}}$$

$$\frac{(3T - T_1)2KA}{l} = \frac{(2T)KA}{2l}$$

$$\Rightarrow 6T - 2T_1 = T$$

$$\Rightarrow 2T_1 = 5T$$

$$\Rightarrow T_1 = \frac{5T}{2} \quad ...(1)$$

Now, equate heat flow rate in $3^{\text{rd}}$ section & total section

$$\frac{T_2 - T}{R_3} = \frac{3T - T}{R_{\text{eq.}}}$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{(T_2 - T)(2KA)}{l} = \frac{2T(KA)}{2l}$$

$$\Rightarrow 2T_2 - 2T = T$$

$$\Rightarrow T_2 = \frac{3T}{2} \quad ...(2)$$

By equation (1) and equation (2)

$$\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{5T \times 2}{2 \times 3T} = \frac{5}{3}$$

solution:
Using first law of thermodynamics

$\Delta Q$ is same

$\Delta U$ is also same

$P$ is also same

$$= \frac{3}{4}$$

question: The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a Hydrogen atom when it undergoes $\text{n} = 2 \rightarrow \text{n} = 3$ and $\text{n} = 4 \rightarrow \text{n} = 6$ transitions, respectively, is
solution:
$$\Delta\text{E} = \frac{\text{hc}}{\lambda} = \text{E}_{\text{final}} - \text{E}_{\text{initial}} \quad \left(\text{E}_{\text{n}} = \frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{\text{n}^2}\right)$$

$$\Delta\text{E}_{2\rightarrow 3} = \frac{\text{hc}}{\lambda_{2\rightarrow 3}} = \text{E}_3 - \text{E}_2 = \frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{3^2} - \left(\frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{2^2}\right)$$
$$= \text{R}_{\text{H}} \left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}\right)$$
$$= \text{R}_{\text{H}} \times \frac{5}{36}$$

$$\therefore \lambda_{2\rightarrow 3} = \frac{\text{hc} \cdot 36}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 5}$$

$$\Delta\text{E}_{4\rightarrow 6} = \text{E}_6 - \text{E}_4 = \frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{36} + \frac{\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{16} = \frac{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \times 20}{36 \times 16}$$

$$\frac{\text{hc}}{\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6}} = \frac{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \times 20}{36 \times 16}$$

$$\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6} = \frac{\text{hc} \times 36 \times 16}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 20}$$

$$\frac{\lambda_{2\rightarrow 3}}{\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6}} = \frac{\frac{\text{hc} \cdot 36}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 5}}{\frac{\text{hc} \times 36 \times 16}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 20}}$$
$$= \frac{1}{4}$$
